summary: Wave 3: make each role's server access match the modules its sidebar grants (UI-06..UI-15, HR-R8), then adversarially review and fix

built.summary:
UI-06 is fixed for every route in my modules. The marketing and brand_manager roles were refused because the reads and writes behind the Marketing workspace allowed MANAGERS only. They now allow MARKETING_TEAM (MANAGERS plus marketing and brand_manager), and company scoping still goes through lib/tenantScope.ts.

Widened routes:
- crm: GET /customers, /customers/:id, /summary, /campaigns, /campaigns/audience, /behavioral-segments, /behavioral-segments/:slug/members; POST /campaigns, /campaigns/:id/send, /behavioral-segments/compute.
- promos: all 5 routes.
- discounts: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE /sections.
- qrcodes: GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE.
- analytics: the funnel, items, search and overview reads.
- marketing: /activity and /team (/team now also lists brand_manager logins).
- loyalty: settings GET/PATCH and the tier routes (GET, POST, PATCH, DELETE).

Scoping tightened while widening:
- analytics: the 4 reads used to filter on the raw `req.staffUser.tenantFilter`. They now use conceptWhere/conceptIdsInScope: a foreign conceptId returns 404 instead of being ignored, and a login with no company sees nothing.
- discounts: GET/PATCH/DELETE /sections also used the raw tenantFilter. They now use conceptIdsInScope (read or write), so a client conceptId can only narrow within the caller's company.

Still guarded (MANAGERS only): bans and strikes (create, reverse, lift), POST /loyalty/earn, and wallet top-ups (wallet module, not mine). In the admin, the wallet top-up and Block/Unblock buttons on /crm, and the forgive-strike and lift-ban buttons on /crm/naughty-list, now show to manager roles only (role from GET /permissions/me).

Remaining blocker outside my files: GET /concepts still returns 403 for marketing and brand_manager. Every marketing page calls it for its brand picker; the exact change is in needsOtherFiles.

items.id: UI-06 marketing/brand_manager reads (crm customers/summary/campaigns/segments, promos, analytics/*, marketing activity/team, loyalty settings/tiers, discounts/sections, qrcodes)
items.note: Every read from crawl-marketing-d.json in my modules now returns 200 for both roles (tested). Company scoping is unchanged, and the analytics and discounts reads are now tighter (see summary).

items.id: UI-06 marketing normal writes (campaigns create+send, segment recompute, promos, section discounts, QR codes, loyalty settings+tiers)
items.note: Open to MARKETING_TEAM. Creates bind to the active company. A brand from another company on create returns 404 (tested).

items.id: UI-06 foh_management gets what crm/campaigns/complaints/reviews promise
items.note: foh_management is already in MANAGERS, so every crm and campaign route was already open to it. The crawl showed no crm 403s, and the test confirms 200 on the crm and campaign reads.

items.id: UI-06 boh_management must not gain crm
items.note: I added nothing for boh_management. It is still in MANAGERS, so it already reaches the crm routes. Closing that is left to the cross-cutting module gate (crm is not in GATED_PREFIXES).

items.id: UI-06 GET /concepts 403 for marketing (brand picker on every marketing page)
items.note: In backend/src/modules/concepts/routes.ts, which I don't own. Exact change in needsOtherFiles.

items.id: UI-06 frontend buttons for actions marketing keeps 403 on
items.note: On /crm, wallet top-up and Block/Unblock are hidden for non-managers. On /crm/naughty-list, forgive-strike and lift-ban are hidden for non-managers.

built.judgementCalls:
1. Sending a campaign (POST /crm/campaigns/:id/send) is opened to marketing and brand_manager. They own the Marketing workspace (ownerRoles) and campaigns is in their defaults, so sending is their job. Limits that still apply: send goes only to the campaign's own company audience (opt-outs and bans respected). Sending to the servd-level new-brand waitlist still needs the campaigns module. If you want a second sign-off before a broadcast, that is new work (a submit/approve step), not a role change.
2. Customer data: marketing and brand_manager now read the CRM customer list and customer detail (name, phone, email, spend, wallet balance, loyalty) for their own company. The bulk-read PII flag (pii_export_row_threshold) still fires for them. No customer export endpoint exists in crm. The waitlist CSV is in the waitlist module, already gated by the crm/campaigns module and untouched.
3. Manual wallet credits (POST /wallet/topup and /wallet/bulk-topup) stay MANAGERS (money to one customer), and the button is hidden for marketing.
4. The manual loyalty points back-fill (POST /loyalty/earn) stays MANAGERS (points into one customer's account).
5. Bans and strikes stay MANAGERS: they decide who may order or book, which is an operations call. Covers POST /crm/bans, POST /crm/bans/:id/lift, POST /crm/strikes and POST /crm/strikes/:id/reverse. Marketing can still read the naughty list and the bans list (those were already open to all staff), and the action buttons are hidden for them.
6. Loyalty programme settings (earn/redeem rates, expiry, minimum redeem) and the tier ladder are opened to marketing. This is programme design that changes future loyalty liability, but it moves no money to anyone. Settings and tiers are per company and pinned to the active company.
7. Pricing levers are opened to marketing: promo codes (including 100%-off percentage codes), timed section discounts and QR codes. These are the promos module in their defaults. Promos keep their per-company unique code and value checks.
8. /marketing/team now lists brand_manager logins as well as marketing (both are members of the workspace). It shows names, emails and last marketing action only.
9. Analytics and discount reads behave slightly differently now:
   - A foreign conceptId on /analytics/items and /analytics/search now returns 404. Before, it silently fell back to all brands.
   - A user with no company now sees nothing. Before, they could match brands with no company.
   - These reads now follow the admin's global brand picker, like other pages.
built.tests:
New test: backend/tests/wave3Marketing.test.ts, 13 tests, all passing. It runs the real auth middleware with two companies plus a marketing login that has no company, and checks:
- Every marketing read returns 200 for marketing and brand_manager.
- foh_management can read crm and campaigns.
- The workspace writes (campaign create/send with WhatsApp and email stubbed, promos, discounts, QR codes, loyalty settings and tiers) bind to company A.
- Company B's marketing login gets 404 on company A's rows and brands (15 routes), and sees none of A's rows in lists.
- The login with no company sees nothing.
- Bans, strikes, wallet top-ups and /loyalty/earn still return 403 for the marketing roles.
- A cashier still gets 403 on the whole workspace.

Existing tests for these modules all pass: auditLedgerLoyalty, auditOnlineCheckout, customersReconcile, discountsPublic, sepContent, sepCrm, waitlist and wave3Marketing — 8 files, 142 tests. They ran against database servd_test_w3a with Redis db 22.

`npx tsc --noEmit -p .` is clean in backend (0 errors) and shows no errors in frontend/admin for app/crm.
built.needsOtherFiles:
backend/src/modules/concepts/routes.ts, function conceptView(): the plain GET /concepts and GET /concepts/:id still throw 403 for marketing and brand_manager. These are not managers or cashiers, so they only get through with ?view=storefront. Every Marketing page I opened calls plain '/concepts' for its brand picker: /promos, /discounts, /qrcodes, /analytics, /crm/campaigns, and also /marketing/brands with ?includeInactive=1. So the pickers stay empty and a 403 toast still shows.

Exact change: in conceptView(), after `if (isManager(su.role)) return 'full'`, add
`if (su.role === 'marketing' || su.role === 'brand_manager') return 'full'`
The reason is that both roles hold the `brands` module ("The one brand editor", /marketing/brands), which needs the full row and includeInactive. The list stays company-scoped through resolveTenantScope/tenantWhere.

If the owner of that file prefers not to expose the full row, the minimum my pages need is a narrow view for those two roles: id, tenantId, name, slug, isActive, logoUrl, primaryColor (like TILL_CONCEPT_SELECT minus the tax fields). In that case the brand editor's PATCH /concepts/:id (MANAGERS) needs a separate decision by the brands stream.

review.title: POST /crm/campaigns/:id/send has no claim, so a campaign can be broadcast again (and twice at once). This is now open to marketing and brand_manager
review.scenario: I reproduced this on DB servd_test_w3a_rv. A brand_manager created a campaign and fired two concurrent POST /crm/campaigns/:id/send, then a third after the broadcast finished. All three returned 200, and 3 CampaignSend rows (3 WhatsApp messages) went to the same customer. The route never checks campaign.status. Status only becomes 'sent' when the background loop ends. In /crm/campaigns the 'Send now' button is hidden only when status === 'sent', so it reappears as soon as the first mutation resolves, while the broadcast is still running. One extra click re-sends to the company's whole audience through the WhatsApp gateway. Before this wave only MANAGERS could hit this; it is now the marketing roles' everyday button.
review.fix: Claim the campaign atomically before counting or sending: `const claimed = await prisma.campaign.updateMany({ where: { id: campaign.id, status: 'draft' }, data: { status: 'sent', sentAt: new Date() } }); if (claimed.count === 0) throw new AppError('CAMPAIGN_ALREADY_SENT', 'This campaign has already been sent', 409)`. Write only recipientCount at the end of the loop. Add a test: two concurrent sends give one 200 and one 409, with CampaignSend count = audience size; a re-send after completion gives 409.

review.title: The CRM reads newly opened to marketing roles show another company's spend, order count, brand and wallet for shared customers
review.scenario: Reproduced: the customer ordered 5x PKR 20,000 at company A's 'Secret A Brand' and once at company B (rollup totalSpentCents 9,999,900, walletBalance 77,700, preferredConceptId = A's brand). GET /crm/customers and GET /crm/customers/:id as company B's marketing login return totalSpentCents 9999900, _count.orders 6, walletBalance 77700 and preferredConcept {name:'Secret A Brand', slug:...}. safeCustomerSelect returns the global rollups (the file's own comment at companyCustomerStats says they are global across companies), `_count: { orders: true }` is unfiltered and preferredConcept is not scoped. GET /crm/behavioral-segments/:slug/members (getSegmentsWithMembers) also returns global totalSpentCents/lastOrderAt/walletBalance. Managers already had this; wave 3 extends it to two more roles. The standing rule says a newly admitted role must never see another company's rows. The wave3Marketing test only uses customers who ordered at one company, so it cannot catch this.
review.fix: In /customers, /customers/:id and the segment-members select, replace totalSpentCents/firstOrderAt/lastOrderAt/_count.orders with per-company figures from the existing companyCustomerStats(await conceptIdsInScope(req,'read'), ids) helper. Return preferredConcept only when its tenantId is in scope (else null). Decide whether walletBalance (a global wallet) belongs on a company-scoped CRM page. Add a two-company test with a customer who ordered at both companies, asserting company B's marketing sees only B's spend/count and no A brand name.

review.title: The widened non-/crm routes are not module-gated, so the CEO's Module Access cannot close them for marketing roles
review.scenario:
Reproduced: I saved RoleModuleAccess for marketing as ['marketing_workspace','calendar'] (CEO unticked crm, promos, analytics) and called invalidateModuleAccessCache(). Results for company B's marketing login:
- GET /crm/customers → 403 (/crm is gated)
- POST /promos with a 100%-off percentage code → 201
- PATCH /loyalty/settings → 200
- GET /analytics/overview → 200
/discounts/sections, /qrcodes and /marketing/* are the same: GATED_PREFIXES has no entry for /promos, /discounts, /qrcodes, /loyalty/settings|tiers, /analytics or /marketing. Before this wave the role arrays refused marketing outright. Now the role array admits them and the module toggle (decision 34: 'module access is THE control') does nothing. This is the 'opens a page outside its modules by URL' half of UI-06, re-created for the pricing and loyalty-liability levers.

review.title: Five Marketing pages still 403 on GET /concepts, and the proposed fix opens the full brand row when a narrow picker view already exists
review.scenario: /promos, /discounts, /qrcodes, /analytics and /crm/campaigns all call plain api.get('/concepts'). conceptView() still throws 403 for marketing and brand_manager. The brand pickers stay empty, a red toast shows, and marketing cannot target a brand on a promo, section discount (conceptId is required, so discounts cannot be created at all from the UI), QR code (also requires conceptId) or campaign. UI-06 is therefore not fixed for those pages. The builder's needsOtherFiles change (`return 'full'` for marketing/brand_manager) hands those roles the whole Concept row on both GET /concepts and GET /concepts/:id: tax rates, strn/ntn, fbrPosId/srbPosId (which CLAUDE.md says are edited only on the POS connector page) and every other column. Meanwhile GET /concepts?view=picker (PICKER_CONCEPT_SELECT: id, tenantId, name, slug, logoUrl, primaryColor; any staff; company-scoped; empty scope denies) already serves exactly what these pickers need. Separately, the /marketing/brands editor (module 'brands', in both roles' defaults) still gets 403 on PATCH /concepts/:id (MANAGERS).
review.fix: Switch the five pages to api.get('/concepts?view=picker') with a distinct queryKey (e.g. ['concepts','picker']) so they do not share cache with pages that need the full row. Then no change to concepts/routes.ts is needed for them. Treat the /marketing/brands full-row read and PATCH as a separate owner decision, not bundled into conceptView.

review.title: wave3Marketing.test.ts does not prove some of what it claims
review.scenario:
Four gaps:
(a) The separation tests use customers who ordered at one company only, so the cross-company aggregate leak (W3A-RV-02) passes.
(b) PATCH /loyalty/settings is sent with {}, so it does not check that the value lands in company A's settings or that company B's settings are unchanged. The 'binds to company A' claim is untested for settings.
(c) There is no double-send or re-send test for the newly opened campaign send (W3A-RV-01).
(d) There is no saved Module Access override case, so it does not check that the CEO can still close the widened routes (W3A-RV-03).

review.title: The /discounts category picker calls a route that does not exist and gets 404 for every role (pre-existing)
review.scenario: Line 50 queries `/menu/categories?conceptId=…`. menu/routes.ts has no GET /categories, so the request matches GET /menu/:conceptId with conceptId='categories', the concept lookup fails and it returns 404. Once a brand can be picked (after W3A-RV-04), marketing still cannot scope a section discount to a menu section from this page, which is the page's purpose.
review.fix: Point the query at GET /menu/:conceptId (the ALL_STAFF menu tree, company-checked) and read its categories. Alternatively add a scoped GET /menu/categories?conceptId= that calls assertConceptOwned(req, conceptId, 'read'). Either way, add a two-company test.

fix.summary: All six findings were real, and I fixed all six in my own files, with tests. The send-once fix also needed one wait condition changed in tests/sepCrm.test.ts. RV-03 I handled differently from the reviewer's proposal: I did not touch moduleAccess.ts. Instead each widened staff route now carries the existing requireModule helper (backend/src/modules/notifications/requireModule.ts), which uses the same source of truth as the central gate (effectiveModulesForUser). All 21 tests in backend/tests/wave3Marketing.test.ts pass, and so do the 11 other test files that touch these routes (211 tests in total). Typecheck is clean for every file I own, in both the backend and the admin.

items.note: In backend/src/modules/crm/routes.ts, POST /crm/campaigns/:id/send now claims the campaign before counting or sending anything. The claim is a single updateMany with where {id, status in [draft, scheduled]} and data {status: sent, sentAt}; if it matches nothing the route returns 409 CAMPAIGN_ALREADY_SENT. If the audience count throws after the claim, the campaign goes back to its earlier status. The background loop now writes only recipientCount at the end. If the loop crashes, the campaign is marked 'failed' and is never put back to draft, so the people who already got it are not messaged again. In the admin (frontend/admin/src/app/crm/campaigns/page.tsx), 'Send now' shows only for draft and scheduled campaigns, and 'failed' gets its own status colour. Tests: two sends at once give one 200 and one 409 (CAMPAIGN_ALREADY_SENT); CampaignSend rows and the stubbed sendText call count both equal the audience size; a send after the broadcast finishes gives 409 and adds no rows. Removing the claim makes both tests fail. tests/sepCrm.test.ts waited for status 'sent' as its 'broadcast finished' signal; it now waits for recipientCount. Its assertions are unchanged.

safeCustomerSelect no longer returns the global rollups. A new helper, scopedCustomerFigures(), fills in totalSpentCents, firstOrderAt, lastOrderAt and _count.orders from companyCustomerStats over conceptIdsInScope(req,'read'). I added MIN(first order) to that helper. These figures now count completed orders at in-scope brands only; before, _count counted every order at every company. preferredConcept and preferredConceptId are returned only when that brand's tenantId is in scope; otherwise null. walletBalance goes to MANAGERS only and is null for marketing roles. This applies to GET /crm/customers and GET /crm/customers/:id. Segment members (segmentComputation.ts getSegmentsWithMembers plus the route) no longer select the global spend, last order or wallet; the route fills spend and last order from in-scope stats. GET /crm/customers?conceptId= now calls assertConceptOwned(read) first, so filtering by another company's brand is a 404. In the admin, the CRM page shows '—' when walletBalance is null, and walletBalance is removed from the segments page type (it was never displayed). Test: one customer with 5 x PKR 20,000 at A's 'Secret A Brand' and 1 x PKR 123 at company B, global rollups 9,999,900, wallet 77,700 and preferred brand A. Company B's marketing login sees 12,300 / 1 order / B's dates, no brand, no wallet, and none of the strings 'Secret A Brand', 9999900 or 77700, in the list, the profile and the segment members. Company A sees 10,000,000 / 5 orders and its own brand. foh_management still sees the wallet. Removing the fix makes both tests fail.

Each staff route on these modules is guarded by marketingGuard = [requireAuth(...MARKETING_TEAM), requireModule(...)]. /promos and /discounts/sections need promos. /qrcodes needs promos or configuration, because the Configuration hub has a QR tile. /loyalty/settings and /loyalty/tiers need crm or configuration (CRM → Loyalty, plus the hub's Loyalty tile). The four /analytics reads need analytics, and /marketing/* needs marketing_workspace. Public routes are not touched: POST /analytics/events, /qrcodes/:id/scan and /convert, /discounts/active, and the customer loyalty routes. The MANAGERS-only route POST /loyalty/earn is also unchanged. Test: a marketing login in company A with moduleDeny [promos, analytics, marketing_workspace, crm, campaigns] gets 403 on 12 reads and writes, including POST /promos with a 100%-off code and PATCH /loyalty/settings, and nothing is written. The same role with the modules still gets 200. I used a per-login moduleDeny rather than a saved RoleModuleAccess row for the marketing role. Both go through the same effectiveModulesForUser call, and a saved role row would change the marketing role for any other test file running against the same database at the same time.

/promos, /discounts, /qrcodes, /analytics and /crm/campaigns now read GET /concepts?view=picker under the query key ['concepts','picker']. That view returns only the brand fields the pickers need, for any staff role, scoped to the operator's companies, and an empty scope denies. No change to concepts/routes.ts is needed for these pages. I am withdrawing the builder's earlier request to make conceptView return 'full' for marketing and brand_manager (see judgementCalls).

Added all four requested tests, plus tests for RV-02's brand filter and for RV-06. The new cases: a customer shared by both companies, B's figures only; PATCH /loyalty/settings with loyalty.min_redeem_points=4321 as company A's marketing, which A reads back while company B's value is unchanged and is not 4321; concurrent send giving 200 + 409; a send after completion giving 409; a Module Access deny giving 403 with nothing written.

The /discounts category picker now reads GET /menu/:conceptId, the existing menu tree. It is open to every staff role and returns 404 for a brand outside the operator's company. The page maps the result to {id, name, conceptId} under its own query key ['menu', conceptId, 'sections']. I did not add a new /menu/categories route, because the menu tree read already does this job (standing rule on duplicates). Test: company A's marketing gets A's category from /menu/{conceptA}; company B's marketing gets 404; a section discount on that category is 201 and company B cannot see it.

fix.judgementCalls:
1. Wallet balance on CRM pages. The wallet is one servd-wide balance with no company. Managers, who already saw it and are the ones who credit it, still see it. marketing and brand_manager now get null, and the page shows '—'.
2. Order count on the CRM list now counts completed orders at the brands in view, to match the spend figure. Before, _count.orders counted every order in every status at every company.
3. A campaign whose broadcast crashes partway is marked 'failed', not draft, and cannot be sent again from the button, because part of the audience may already have it. Retrying means creating a new campaign. Scheduled campaigns can still be sent (nothing schedules them today).
4. Module gates use the Configuration hub too. /qrcodes is open with promos OR configuration, and loyalty settings/tiers with crm OR configuration, because the Configuration hub links to both pages. Every module whose pages call a route opens it, which is how the central gate works.
5. As the reviewer warned, the new module gates close URL-only access for foh_management, boh_management and fnb_manager. None of them hold promos, analytics or marketing_workspace by default, so they now get 403 on /promos, /discounts, /qrcodes, /analytics and /marketing. foh_management holds crm, so it keeps loyalty settings/tiers. boh_management and fnb_manager lose those too unless they hold configuration. This follows the sidebar = server rule.
6. RV-04: please do not apply the builder's earlier needsOtherFiles change to concepts/routes.ts that would make conceptView return 'full' for marketing and brand_manager. It would hand those roles the whole brand row: tax rates, strn/ntn and fbrPosId/srbPosId, which only the POS connector page should edit. The pickers no longer need it.
7. The /marketing/brands editor is still blocked for both marketing roles, even though they hold the 'brands' module by default. Its full-row GET /concepts and its PATCH /concepts/:id are MANAGERS-only. Whether to open them (and which fields) is an owner decision; I did not bundle it in. Until then, 'brands' in their defaults promises a page they cannot use.
8. Not fixed, pre-existing, not widened in this wave: GET /crm/customers/:id/context (ALL_STAFF, shown in the Reservations guest panel) still returns global figures. These are totalSpentCents, firstOrderAt, lastOrderAt, lastVisitAt, noShowCount, complaintCount, reviewCount, avgReviewRating, walletBalance and an unscoped preferredConcept. Company B staff can see a shared customer's activity at company A. It needs the same per-company treatment, with the owner deciding the VIP badge logic in CustomerContextSidebar.
9. Minor leftovers. The /crm/customers list is still ordered by the global lastOrderAt, so ordering slightly reflects activity at the other company; the cursor pagination on that list was already inconsistent before this wave. Separately, /storefront/admin/promos in storefront/routes.ts (MANAGERS) is a second promo-editing API next to /promos. Under the duplicates rule, the owner should decide which one stays.
fix.tests: Run on DB servd_test_w3a (vitest resets it), with REDIS_URL=redis://127.0.0.1:6379/22 and NODE_ENV=test: npx vitest run of accessControl, auditLedgerLoyalty, auditOnlineCheckout, customersReconcile, discountsPublic, reports, sepContent, sepCrm, storefrontQuickfix, waitlist, wave3Gates and wave3Marketing. Result: 12 files, 211 tests, all pass after the sepCrm wait-condition update; wave3Marketing has 21 tests. Mutation check: allowing the claim to match 'sent', and returning the wallet to every role, made the RV-01 and RV-02 tests fail (4 failures); the file was restored from a backup afterwards. npx tsc --noEmit -p . in backend and in frontend/admin shows no errors in any file I own.
fix.needsOtherFiles:
1. backend/src/modules/concepts/routes.ts: do NOT apply the earlier wave-3 request to make conceptView() return 'full' for marketing and brand_manager. The five Marketing pages now use GET /concepts?view=picker. Opening the /marketing/brands editor (the full-row GET and PATCH /concepts/:id) to the marketing roles is a separate owner decision. If approved, it should go to the marketing roles with an explicit field allow-list that excludes tax rates, strn/ntn and fbrPosId/srbPosId, not the full row.
2. backend/src/lib/moduleAccess.ts (optional): the new module gates for /promos, /discounts/sections, /qrcodes, /loyalty/settings|tiers, /analytics/(funnel|items|search|overview) and /marketing are enforced in the route files through requireModule. If the moduleAccess owner prefers to move them into GATED_PREFIXES, use the same anyOf sets: promos; promos; promos+configuration; crm+configuration; analytics; marketing_workspace. Then drop requireModule from marketingGuard in those six files so the rule is defined in one place.
3. Owner follow-up, not a code change for another agent: GET /crm/customers/:id/context (crm/routes.ts, my file, but outside this wave's widening) still returns global rollups. See judgementCalls 8.

built.summary:
Finance can now open every Finance-workspace page in my modules without a 403, and do the workspace's normal work. HR can read positions, the staff-meal log and tip pools, and can edit positions. Every route I widened still filters by company. Each has a two-company test: company B's finance or HR gets 404 or an empty list on company A's rows, and anything created lands in the active company.

What was already done: the crawl ran at 14:26, before the BOOKS-02 commits at 14:51–14:59. Those commits (in the current code) had already opened reconciliation, exceptions, bank accounts, projections, capex reads and tip pools to finance and HR. I checked each one in the current code and in tests and left them alone.

Opened in this pass:
- **Gift cards (`giftCards/routes.ts`):** finance can list cards. A new `GET /gift-cards/:id/redemptions` shows one card's history, filtered by company. Before, the page sent people to the accounting audit log, which finance cannot open.
- **CapEx and OpEx (`financePlanning/routes.ts`, `opex/routes.ts`):** finance can read and write projects, lines, quotes, instalments, categories and payments. Paid entries post to the ledger in the same transaction, as before. Capitalising, `post-payments` and the OpEx backfill stay CEO-only.
- **Petty cash and deposit drops (`trustops/routes.ts`):** finance can list boxes, open a box, count one, and list or record deposit drops. The box list now includes the custodian's name.
- **Staff meals (`trustops/routes.ts`):** HR can read the log, and each meal now includes the staff member's name.
- **Positions (`positions/routes.ts`, `positions/contributions.ts`):** managers, HR and finance can read seats, the summary, departments, shift bands and contributions. Only managers and HR can edit seats and shift bands. Inter-company contribution writes stay managers-only. I also fixed four bugs here:
  - Department and shift-band lists now return empty when no company is active (they used a non-null assertion on the active company).
  - Creating a shift band with no active company now returns 422.
  - Deleting a position or editing a shift band that belongs to another company now returns 404 instead of a 500.
  - Editing a position now looks the seat up with write scope.
- **Procurement reads (`procurement/routes.ts`):** finance is now let in by role on bills, payments, purchase orders, supplier statements and the 3-way match, and sees every supplier in its company. All procurement writes are unchanged. **Finance still gets 403 on these until `moduleAccess.ts` changes** (change A in needsOtherFiles).

Frontend: buttons the server would refuse are hidden. The reconciliation page hides "Book adjustment" unless the user is CEO or owner, and hides "Close shift" for roles that cannot close a drawer. The capex page shows Capitalise only to the CEO. Tip pools show Post and "Mark paid" only to the CEO and owners. Petty cash works without the staff list: it takes the custodian name from the box, falls back to the signed-in user in the custodian picker, and stops the error toasts. The gift-cards page shows a card's history inline and the audit-log link only to CEO and management. The staff-meals page is now read-only and uses the names sent with each meal. Its "Log meal" button posted to a retired endpoint (410) and is gone.

items.note: Current code (BOOKS-02 commits plus this pass): finance gets 200 on all 25 of the Finance-page reads in my modules (tested). built.judgementCalls:
1. CapEx: finance now works the whole tracker (projects, lines, quotes, instalments). Marking an instalment paid posts an advance, prepayment or fee to the books, as it did for managers. I treated recording a supplier payment in the books as finance's own job. Capitalising onto the fixed-asset register and post-payments stay CEO-only.
2. OpEx: finance can create and edit categories and lines and record payments, which post the expense (owner decision 23). The backfill (post-unposted) stays CEO-only.
3. Petty cash: finance can open boxes and count them. A top-up over a box's limit still needs an approver's PIN from that box's company, whoever records it. Spend and top-up were already open to all staff.
4. Deposit drops: finance can record a drop, which posts Dr bank / Cr cash. I judged cash-to-bank to be finance's work. If only the person carrying the cash should record it, revert POST /trustops/deposit-drops to MANAGERS; the read must stay open.
5. Reconciliation: booking an adjustment journal stays CEO + owners, as BOOKS-02 decided. Finance imports statements and ignores lines, and no longer sees the Book button. Closing a drawer stays with the till roles, and finance no longer sees Close shift.
6. Gift cards: finance can read the register and each card's history. Voiding a card stays with managers because it writes off a customer's balance. Issuing and applying a card were already open to all staff behind the gift_cards module; I did not change that.
7. Tip pools: posting and paying stay CEO + owners. HR, finance and managers draft, review and delete drafts.
8. Positions: the page is in HR's workspace, seat titles are HR designations and departments come from HR Org setup, so HR (and managers) edit seats and shift bands. Finance only reads the labour budget. Inter-company contributions move money between two companies' books, so writes stay MANAGERS (plus the existing check that the editor belongs to both companies).
9. Procurement: finance reads payables only. All creation, approval, receiving, bill entry, voiding and payment stays with the existing roles. Finance now sees every supplier in its company, not only those assigned to it. I noticed owner and fnb_manager are also missing from that 'sees all suppliers' list and did not change it.
10. Staff meals: HR reads the log; finance does not (it holds no staff_directory module). I removed the dead 'Log meal' form, which posted to an endpoint that returns 410.
11. Not changed, for you to decide: /opex, /positions, /trustops and /crosschecks have no module gate. Every manager tier, including FOH/BOH managers who hold neither 'capital' nor 'accounting', can still reach them by URL, exactly as before this pass. A gate is suggested in needsOtherFiles change A.

review.title: Finance and HR newly reach /opex, /trustops (petty cash, deposit drops, staff meals) and /positions even when the CEO has removed their modules
review.scenario: Reproduced on servd_test_w3b_rv with a finance user (company A) whose moduleDeny is ['capital','accounting','gift_cards','payroll']. /finance/capex and /gift-cards correctly answer 403. But GET /opex/categories → 200, POST /opex/categories → 201, GET /trustops/petty-cash/boxes → 200, GET /trustops/deposit-drops → 200, POST /trustops/deposit-drops → 201, GET /positions → 200 (every seat's salary and the filling login's email), GET /positions/summary → 200. That POST /trustops/deposit-drops posts Dr bank / Cr cash, and POST /opex/payments (same OPEX_TEAM guard) posts an expense, so these are ledger writes. The same applies to HR on the seat and shift-band writes (POSITION_EDITORS) and the staff-meal log: unticking staff_directory does not close them. Before this pass these routes were MANAGERS-only, so finance and HR could not reach them whatever their modules were. The widening is new, so it is not 'exactly as before' as judgement call 11 says. Owner decision 34 makes Module Access the control. The builder's test 'a role without the modules is still refused' does not show this: cashier and HR are refused by the role arrays (they are not in FINANCE_TEAM), not by any module gate. No test covers finance or HR with a module removed.

review.title: Finance can now list every customer's gift-card code (a bearer credential) plus recipient emails, and spend any card through the ALL_STAFF redeem
review.scenario: Before this pass GET /gift-cards was MANAGERS-only, so finance could not see codes. Now GIFT_CARD_READERS = FINANCE_TEAM. Reproduced: finance A's GET /gift-cards returns the full rows, including code 'GIFTSECRET…', balanceCents and recipientEmail/buyerEmail. GET /gift-cards/:id/redemptions also returns card.code. POST /gift-cards/redeem is ALL_STAFF (finance holds gift_cards) and needs only the code plus an order of the operator's company. So a finance user can now take any active card's code from the list and drain that customer's balance onto any open order in the company. That is money moving from a specific customer, which the brief says keeps its guard. Finance's job here is reconciling the 2080 liability, and that does not need the bearer code or the customer's email.
review.fix: For roles outside MANAGERS, return a masked code (e.g. '••••' + last 4) and omit buyerEmail and recipientEmail, in both GET /gift-cards and GET /gift-cards/:id/redemptions. Alternatively, keep the redeem engine from accepting a code that was not presented at the till. Add a test that finance's list holds no full code.

review.title: Positions create/patch accepts another company's shiftBandId; the widened seat editors (now HR too) can attach company B's band and read it back
review.scenario: checkSeatRefs() validates departmentId, conceptId and filledByUserId but not shiftBandId. Reproduced: HR in company A sends POST /positions with shiftBandId set to company B's ShiftBand and gets 200. The seat is stored with B's band, and GET /positions (include shiftBand) then returns B's band name and times ('B-secret-night') to company A. PATCH /positions/:id has the same gap. The standing rule says a cross-company attach on create is 422. This route was widened in this pass (POSITION_EDITORS adds hr), and its tests check only conceptId and title.
review.fix: In checkSeatRefs, add: if (body.shiftBandId && !await prisma.shiftBand.findFirst({ where: { id: body.shiftBandId, tenantId, archivedAt: null }, select: { id: true } })) throw new AppError('SHIFT_BAND_NOT_IN_COMPANY', 'That shift band is not in this company', 422). Pass shiftBandId into checkSeatRefs from both POST and PATCH. Add a two-company test: HR A sends POST and PATCH with B's shiftBandId and gets 422.

items.note: Real: /opex, /trustops (petty cash, deposit drops, staff meals) and /positions are not module-gated prefixes, so widening their role arrays let finance and HR in whatever their modules were. I added a module check inside the routes for the roles newly let in, applied to OpEx, petty-cash boxes, deposit drops, the staff-meal log, positions reads and writes, shift-band writes and the contributions list. Tests: finance with capital and accounting unticked gets 403 on 12 OpEx, petty-cash, deposit-drop and positions calls (reads and writes), and nothing is written. HR with staff_directory unticked gets 403 on positions GET, POST, PATCH and DELETE, shift-band POST and the staff-meal log. fnb_manager, which does not hold 'capital', still gets 200 on /opex, /trustops/deposit-drops and /positions.

Real: GIFT_CARD_READERS = FINANCE_TEAM returned full codes and customer emails, and the all-staff redeem accepts any code from the operator's company. Roles outside the manager tiers now get the code masked to '••••' plus its last 4, with buyerEmail, recipientEmail, buyerCustomerId and message blanked, in both GET /gift-cards and GET /gift-cards/:id/redemptions. Real: checkSeatRefs did not check shiftBandId. It now requires a band of the seat's company (422 SHIFT_BAND_NOT_IN_COMPANY), and a new band must not be archived. A PATCH may re-send the seat's current band even after it is archived, because the edit form always sends shiftBandId. Two-company test: HR A sending company B's band gets 422 on POST and on PATCH, the seat is unchanged, and B's band name never appears in A's /positions. A's own band works; a newly chosen archived band is refused; re-sending the seat's existing archived band is accepted.

fix.judgementCalls:
1. I added the Module Access check inside my own route files instead of the central GATED_PREFIXES list, because moduleAccess.ts is not my file. The check covers only the roles this pass newly let in (finance, and HR). The manager tiers pass exactly as before. Two reasons: (a) before this pass they had no module check on these routes; (b) not every manager tier holds the module behind the page. For example fnb_manager has 'accounting' but not 'capital', so a central '/opex' → capital rule would take OpEx away from fnb_manager. Narrowing the manager tiers is your call, not a side effect of this fix.

2. Which module each route needs:
- OpEx: 'capital', the module the OpEx page sits under.
- Petty cash and deposit drops: 'accounting', the module the sidebar puts those pages under.
- Staff meals: 'staff_directory'.
- Reading positions: 'staff_directory' (HR's Workforce → Positions) or 'capital' (finance's CapEx → Workforce and the OpEx payroll budget).
- Editing positions and shift bands: 'staff_directory' only. Finance still cannot edit seats.

3. Unlike the central gate, which lets requests through if the module lookup errors, these checks refuse on any error. These are back-office pages and no sale or kitchen ticket waits on them.

4. Gift cards: roles outside the manager tiers (in practice finance) see the code as '••••' plus its last 4. The buyer and recipient emails, the buyer customer id and the gift message are blanked. The recipient's name stays visible so finance can tell the cards apart. Managers see the full register as before. The all-staff redeem is unchanged: a code shown at the till still works. Issuing a card is also unchanged (all staff, which was already true before this pass).

5. Positions: a seat already on a band that was later archived can still be saved when the edit form re-sends that band. A newly chosen archived band, or any band from another company, is refused with 422.

6. Not changed, worth knowing: GET /positions still includes the filling login's email (filledBy.email) and every seat's salary for finance and HR. That is the salary budget their pages are built on. Say if you want the email dropped for non-managers.

fix.needsOtherFiles: Optional, not needed for these fixes (the checks now live in my route files): backend/src/lib/moduleAccess.ts GATED_PREFIXES could carry the same rules centrally once you decide whether the manager tiers should be narrowed too. The rules would be { prefix: '/opex', anyOf: ['capital'] }, { prefix: '/positions', anyOf: ['staff_directory','capital'] }, { prefix: '/trustops/petty-cash/boxes', anyOf: ['accounting'] } (deliberately the /boxes path, so /trustops/petty-cash/movements stays open to all staff), { prefix: '/trustops/deposit-drops', anyOf: ['accounting'] }, { prefix: '/trustops/staff-meals', anyOf: ['staff_directory'] }. Caveat before landing: fnb_manager has no 'capital', so it would lose /opex. foh_management has no 'accounting', so it would lose petty-cash boxes and deposit drops. boh_management has no 'capital', so it would lose /opex; its 'staff_directory' keeps it on /positions. If these rules land, the per-route checks in my files become redundant but harmless.
